scenes.heading: Freshness & Latency
scenes.subheading: How current must the data be?
scenes.narration: Freshness and latency objectives answer a deceptively simple question: how up to date does your data need to be to stay useful?

scenes.heading: Two different clocks

right.title: Latency
points: Example: event to table in 5 min

scenes.narration: Freshness measures how old the newest available data is, answering whether a dashboard reflects the last hour or last week. Latency measures how long a single event takes to travel from source to serving layer. They are related but distinct, because a low-latency pipeline that stalls overnight still produces stale data.

scenes.heading: Setting the objective
bullets: Anchor the target to a real business decision
Different tables can carry different freshness tiers
Track the gap between now and the latest partition
Alert on staleness before consumers notice
scenes.narration: Anchor every target to a decision someone actually makes, so you do not over-engineer freshness nobody needs. Different tables deserve different tiers, since a fraud model needs seconds while a monthly report tolerates hours. Track the gap between the current time and the newest partition, and alert on that gap before your consumers ever notice.

scenes.heading: A freshness check
scenes.code:
-- Fail if the newest record is older than the objective
SELECT
  MAX(event_time) AS latest_event,
  NOW() - MAX(event_time) AS staleness,
  CASE
    WHEN NOW() - MAX(event_time) > INTERVAL '60 minutes'
      THEN 'BREACH'
    ELSE 'OK'
  END AS freshness_status
FROM events_serving;
scenes.narration: This check finds the newest event time in the serving table and compares its age against the objective. If the newest record is older than sixty minutes, the status flips to breach. Wiring this into your monitor turns an abstract freshness objective into a concrete pass or fail signal.

scenes.text: Freshness and latency are only meaningful when tied to a decision — set tiers per table and alert on staleness proactively.
scenes.narration: Freshness and latency only matter relative to a decision, so tier them per table and alert on staleness before anyone downstream feels it.
